clue.text: More work the ideal solution

definitions.meaning: Sir Thomas More's best-known book describes an imaginary perfect island state
a perfect, idealised scheme for society

explanation.surface: A further piece of work turns out to be the perfect answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' looks like a comparative, but it is Sir Thomas More, author of the 1516 book.
explanation.definitionFit: The book's title has become the general word for a perfect imagined state, an ideal answer to society's ills.

clue.text: Deceitful company confronted

parts.note: from the saying two's company, three's a crowd
faced means confronted

explanation.surface: A business that met its critics head-on is accused of dishonesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two's company' is the proverb behind company giving TWO.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone two-faced is a hypocrite, showing one face and hiding another, so deceitful.

clue.text: Do a strip, unusually expert at taking off

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of do a strip are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A performer strips off in an unusual act, apparently skilled at removing clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' suggests undressing, matching the strip, but it means mimicking.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking off is imitating mockingly, and a skilled mimic of styles is a parodist.

clue.text: Greek hero in a match takes heartless fellow on

parts.note: a match is a game, with the article kept

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word for fellow is removed

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A Greek warrior in a contest takes on a cruel opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the A out of MAN, leaving MN.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of Mycenae led the Greek forces at Troy, a hero of Homer's epic.

clue.text: Key or lock in castle

parts.note: F is a musical key
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Something about a key or lock found in a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' and 'lock' suggest a door, but the key is musical F and the lock is hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle is a fortified stronghold, a synonym.

clue.text: Left type not required by Kipling's fastest journeyer

definitions.meaning: a sympathiser with communism who is not a party member

definitions.text: not required by Kipling's fastest journeyer
definitions.meaning: Kipling wrote that he travels the fastest who travels alone, so a companion on the road is not needed

explanation.surface: A left-winger has no place in Kipling's line about the quickest traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A political sympathiser is said to travel with the party, and a literal companion on a trip travels alongside.

clue.text: "Little Nell" being performed in state capital

parts.note: Nell Trent is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop
a play being performed is on

explanation.surface: A stage version of Little Nell is playing in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Nell is Dickens's heroine, whose surname is Trent.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of New Jersey.

clue.text: Indicate quarters in strange device

indicators.note: in puts the quarters inside the rearranged letters
strange signals the letters of device are put in an odd order

parts.note: E and N are compass points, or quarters

explanation.surface: Point out the quarters of some peculiar gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' scrambles the clue's device, and 'in' sets the two quarters, east and north, inside it; 'quarters' are compass points, not coins or rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to show or point to something is to give proof of it, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Prominence, say, surrounding right Conservative

indicators.note: surrounding means the word say goes around the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
a lien is a legal right over property

explanation.surface: Prominence, for instance, around a right-wing Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the usual for-example marker, but it is the word SAY itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Salience is the quality of standing out, so prominence is a synonym.

clue.text: Certainly not quick, it helps to make fast entrance

definitions.meaning: quick in its old sense means alive, and the idiom dead as a ... means certainly not alive

definitions.text: it helps to make fast entrance
definitions.meaning: a stud fixing the boards of a door, making the entrance secure

explanation.surface: Something slow that helps secure a door.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom dead as a doornail means utterly lifeless, and such a stud fastens a doorway.

clue.text: Replacement for arbitrator indisposed

parts.note: a ref (referee) arbitrates
indisposed means ill

explanation.surface: A stand-in is needed for a sick referee.
explanation.definitionFit: A refill is a fresh supply put in to take the place of one used up.

clue.text: Novelist that is to leave port in California

parts.note: George Sand was a French novelist
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A writer is set to depart from a Californian harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is a major naval port in southern California.

clue.text: Divine female produces one note, then another

parts.note: A is a musical note
taken as written
E is another musical note

explanation.surface: A goddess sings one note and then a second.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Greek goddess of wisdom, a female deity.

clue.text: Authority contains disturbance

indicators.note: disturbance tells us to disturb the letters of contains

explanation.surface: Those in power keep unrest in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' looks like a verb linking the words, but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanction means official permission, so it is authority granted.

clue.text: Terrifying position above part of house

parts.note: over is the position above something
a wing is a part of a house, here with the article a

explanation.surface: A frightening position on top of a section of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: To overawe is to intimidate with fear or respect, so it is daunting.

clue.text: Prepare to publish selections from submitted items?

indicators.note: selections from says the letters are taken from within submitted items

explanation.surface: An editor chooses pieces from submissions to get them ready for print.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare text for publication is to revise and correct it, an editor's job.

clue.text: Support for old-fashioned union contract

definitions.meaning: taking up a cause, adopting or backing it
a dated term for a betrothal or marriage agreement

explanation.surface: Backing for an old-style trade union agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousing a cause is supporting it, and the old word also meant betrothal or marriage.

clue.text: Badly in love, is in a state

parts.note: ill means badly
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone hopelessly in love is in a terrible condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Illinois is one of the American states.

clue.text: Viscount caught by Turkish governor quails

definitions.note: plural birds; the answer is the collective noun for a group of them

indicators.note: caught by means the viscount's letter is held inside the governor

parts.note: a bey was a provincial governor in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: A nobleman seized by an Ottoman official trembles in fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quails' looks like a verb meaning cowers; it is the plural of the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of quails is called a bevy, the collective noun.

clue.text: Saintly John, a rich gentleman of Padua

parts.note: St John the Baptist
St John the Baptist

explanation.surface: Holy John, a wealthy man from the Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Baptista Minola is the rich father of Katherina in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew, set in Padua; the A is shared with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's comedy the wealthy Paduan father is called Baptista.

clue.text: Artist's description of Romeo and Juliet

definitions.meaning: the lovers came from Verona, so the word for a native of that city describes them

explanation.surface: How a painter would portray Shakespeare's lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: The painter took his name from his birthplace Verona, and the lovers were natives of that city.

clue.text: Artist entered privately

parts.note: entered means came in, written here in inverted order as in came
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter came in quietly, without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the pieces as 'in came RA': the artist entered.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in a closed chamber, so proceedings held privately.

clue.text: Inventory, also, that is including final letter

parts.note: item is an old word for also, used in listing

indicators.note: including means the abbreviation for that is holds the final letter inside

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
Z is the final letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A list, also including the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To list things one by one is to make an inventory of them; both are verbs here.

clue.text: Young Dickensian in more demanding role

definitions.text: Young Dickensian in more demanding role

parts.words: Young Dickensian in more demanding role
parts.note: Dickens's workhouse orphan who famously asks for more gruel, so his part is literally one of demanding more

explanation.surface: A young actor takes on a tougher part in a Dickens adaptation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's orphan boy is remembered for asking the master for a second bowl of gruel.

clue.text: Insistent demand for engagement by old flame

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
an engagement is a battle, action

explanation.surface: An ex insists on an engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' and 'old flame' suggest romance, but engagement is a military action.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaction is a forceful demand, as of a payment.

clue.text: Point to top that's wooden

parts.note: S is a compass point, south
a lid is a top

explanation.surface: Indicate the top that is made of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden here means impassive and unemotional, like a stolid person.

clue.text: Province of Ireland …

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Province of Ireland …' is only the definition; its wordplay (anagram of LISTENER, 'this magazine circulates') lies in 24-across's clue, which the check cannot quote across entries

clue.text: …this magazine circulates in

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as '…this magazine circulates in' anagrams the answer to 23-across (LEINSTER), whose words are in another entry's clue and cannot be quoted here

clue.text: Chasing tool that's more important

definitions.meaning: chasing is engraving metal, done with a burin

explanation.surface: A hunting implement that matters more.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraver's cutting tool is called a burin or graver, and graver is also the comparative of grave, serious.
